name: QE24 Dynamic Page Probe
author: HackHub Quest Editor
description: QA probe for SDK 0.24 dynamic website pages, r246 rebuild: one static control page and seven dynamic pages on qe24-dyn.test. Compared with 1.0.0 the beat is now fired by the 'qedyn beat' terminal command instead of an Http.Response that never arrives (r241/r242), Http.Response is logged BEFORE any host filter so 'no event' and 'unexpected host' can be told apart, and /form now prints what Mail.send returned and offers a second button that goes through the documented Events.emit bridge (r245: the quest's own mail arrives, a page's does not). Type 'qedyn status' for everything the probe recorded. Claim QEDynProbeQuest and follow its objectives - they are the QA checklist. Nothing auto-starts. 1.1.1 (r247): the qedyn command is now built inside a guarded block so it can never stop the mod from loading, and gains 'qedyn claim' - mod quest posts have stopped surfacing on the feed (docs/03 §21), so the quest can be claimed straight from the terminal instead. 1.4.0 (r250): the correction - builds 1.0 to 1.3 sent their test mails to player@gomail.com, a placeholder from this repo's own QA project that has never existed, so the mail that never arrived proved nothing. Every probe mail now goes to the player (no to: field, or the real address from Mail.getPlayerEmail) or nowhere on purpose, clearly labelled. That re-opens the real question the whole probe was built for: can a page's own script send a mail that actually arrives?
